column1: #   tier   ban   = clear anti-pattern; fix by default
#          watch = review each hit by hand; many are legitimate in context
#   only   optional: comma-separated extensions the pattern applies to
#          (e.g. py, java, yaml) or exact file names (an entry with a dot, e.g.
#          CMakeLists.txt). Omit, or write - when an `if` column follows, to
#   if     optional: an ERE the same file must also match for its hits to count
#          (e.g. a framework import, so a Spring-only rule skips Quarkus files).
#   regex  GNU grep -E (ERE). No backreferences: scan.sh wraps each regex in
#          an extra group when excerpting long lines, which shifts numbering.
# CONSERVATIVE BY DESIGN. Only high-signal, low-false-positive anti-patterns
# live here. Everything nuanced (missing response_model, wrong probe choice,
# missing resources:, field injection) is NOT grepped — it lives in the
# per-stack checklists in ../references/ for the reviewer to read.
# Idioms and rewrites for every pattern: ../references/<stack>-idioms.md
# Project-specific anti-patterns go in a separate file passed with --patterns.

column3: Pydantic v1 API in a v2 project
kind: Pod (prefer a Deployment for long-running workloads)
secret in a plain env value:
sun.misc.Signal handler (use graceful shutdown + lifecycle hooks)
javax.* Jakarta EE import (Jakarta EE 11 uses jakarta.*)
Jackson 2 databind/core import in Spring code (Boot 4 uses tools.jackson)
hand-written health endpoint in Spring (use Actuator probes)
JdbcTemplate (prefer a Spring Data repository, or JdbcClient for SQL-shaped work)
hand-written health endpoint in ASP.NET Core (use MapHealthChecks)
hand-built Npgsql data source/connection (EF Core, or AddNpgsqlDataSource)
io/ioutil (deprecated since Go 1.16; use io / os)
fmt.Print* (log/slog in services; fine as a CLI's stdout)
naked new / delete (prefer RAII and smart pointers)
using namespace std in a header
iostream / printf logging in service code (use spdlog)
